title: Tata Steel to sell tubes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for ₹28,000 crore
dek: APL Apollo will pay up to ₹11,700 crore for the tubes business and ₹16,300 crore for the colour-coated steel unit. The linked deals need competition and shareholder approval and should close by March 2028.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Tata Steel will sell its steel tubes business and its colour-coated steel subsidiary to APL Apollo Tubes for up to ₹28,000 crore, the two companies told the stock exchanges on Sunday after their boards approved the deals. Shares of both companies were expected to react when trading opens on Monday.

The package has two parts, according to the companies' disclosures. APL Apollo will buy Tata Steel's tubes and pipes business for a lump-sum cash payment of up to ₹11,700 crore through a slump sale, in which the business is transferred as a going concern. It will also buy all of Tata Steel Colors Private Limited, formerly Tata BlueScope Steel, for ₹16,300 crore. Tata Steel holds half of Tata Steel Colors directly and its wholly owned subsidiary Tata Steel Downstream Products holds the other half, so each will receive ₹8,150 crore.

## What is being sold

The tubes business, which has plants at Jamshedpur, Hosur, Khopoli and Sahibabad, along with certain cold-rolling and coated-steel facilities at Khopoli, had a turnover of about ₹11,375 crore in 2025-26, or 8.14% of Tata Steel's standalone turnover, according to the filing as reported. Its net worth was about ₹3,274 crore at the end of March 2026. The division crossed one million tonnes of production and sales in 2024-25, Tata Steel said at the time.

Tata Steel Colors makes colour-coated steel and building products. It had a turnover of about ₹4,680 crore and a profit after tax of ₹85 crore in 2025-26, according to reports of the disclosure.

## Why they are doing it

Tata Steel said the sale would unlock value from the tubes business and rationalise its downstream portfolio, according to reports. For APL Apollo, India's largest maker of structural steel tubes, the deal adds capacity, distribution reach and new products in tubes and colour-coated steel, which go into construction, infrastructure and housing.

The two transactions depend on each other and are meant to close at the same time. They need approval from the Competition Commission of India and from APL Apollo's shareholders for the Tata Steel Colors purchase, as well as other regulatory approvals, and are expected to be completed on or before 31 March 2028.

## What it means

For Tata Steel, the sale shrinks its own downstream presence in tubes and coated products while the steel that goes into them is made in its plants. The company is spending heavily on lower-emission steelmaking, including a scrap-based electric arc furnace it opened in India this year and a planned decarbonisation project in the Netherlands, according to its own releases.

For APL Apollo, the purchase combines two of the biggest brands in Indian steel tubes. The Competition Commission will review the deal before it can close; the companies have not said how APL Apollo will fund the payments.

## Key numbers

- ₹28,000 crore: total value of the two deals
- ₹11,700 crore: cash for the tubes business (slump sale)
- ₹16,300 crore: for 100% of Tata Steel Colors, split equally between Tata Steel and Tata Steel Downstream Products
- ₹11,375 crore: tubes business turnover in 2025-26, 8.14% of Tata Steel's standalone turnover
- ₹4,680 crore: Tata Steel Colors turnover in 2025-26; profit after tax ₹85 crore
- 31 March 2028: latest date for completion

Indian markets are open on Monday and closed on Tuesday, 24 November, for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
